Nebraska's operative SNAP policy manual is Title 475 of the Nebraska Administrative Code (475 NAC), cited by a bare numbered-section convention such as '3-003.01H3' (Chapter 3, Eligibility, section 003.01, subsection H3). This pack also cites a real Nebraska Revised Statute, Neb. Rev. Stat. § 68-1017.02, for the drug-felony and ABAWD-waiver-bar findings, so this pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'NRS 68-', matching this roster's Connecticut, Kentucky, Alabama, and Louisiana packs' multi-family pattern.

patterns.note: Nebraska DHHS SNAP Policy Manual, Title 475 NAC, cited by bare chapter-section-subsection number, e.g. 3-003.01H (Utility Allowance), 3-003.01H3 (One Utility Allowance), 3-003.01H1b (SUA Eligibility).

Nebraska Revised Statutes, Chapter 68 (Public Assistance), cited by section number. This pack cites exactly one: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 68-1017.02, the drug-felony modified-ban and ABAWD-waiver-bar statute.

nenac.note: Utility Allowance — chapter overview: household may receive one of SUA, LUA, OUA, or Telephone Standard Allowance; lists non-allowable utility costs
Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) — heating or cooling costs billed on a recurring, separate basis, or anticipated NLIEAP energy-assistance payment

Eligibility for Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) — clarifies 'recurring' expense standard, qualifying cooling systems (a/c, evaporative cooler, room units — not a fan), non-qualifying supplemental heat sources (space heaters, electric blankets, heat lamps, cooking stoves)
Limited Utility Allowance (LUA) — household billed for at least TWO utilities other than heating/cooling (telephone, water, sewer, garbage/trash, well/septic maintenance, non-heating gas/electric)
One Utility Allowance (OUA) — household billed for EXACTLY ONE utility other than heating/cooling and other than telephone; cannot combine with SUA or Telephone Allowance eligibility
Telephone Allowance — household billed for basic telephone service fee (landline), or a cell phone used as the primary phone when no house phone is available

nenrs.note: SNAP eligibility — drug-felony modified ban, subsection (1)(b): permanent ineligibility only for (i) three or more felony convictions for possession/use of a controlled substance, or (ii) any felony conviction for sale/distribution/intent to sell or distribute; individuals with one or two possession/use felony convictions remain eligible while participating in or after completing a state-licensed or nationally accredited substance-abuse treatment program since the conviction date. ALSO bars DHHS from seeking, applying for, accepting, or renewing an area-wide ABAWD work-requirement waiver except where expressly required by federal law. A 2025 bill (LB319) that would have replaced the drug-felony provision with a broader rule was vetoed and the veto was sustained — this statute's text is UNCHANGED as of this pack's fetch date.
